title: Hybrid Batch Normalisation: Resolving the Dilemma of Batch Normalisation in Federated Learning
summary: The pinned released collection path stores hybrid moments instead of raw moments, defeating the central exact-statistics claim. Two local manuscript errors are also demonstrated.
limitations: No author-code execution or fresh empirical reproduction.
Historical experiment revision and numerical effects unverified.
No separate OpenReview supplement acquired; Appendix A-B are present in the original.
Other repository files were not inspected.

claim.location: Abstract; page 2 contribution 1; pages 4-5 Section 3.2, Equations (7)-(8); page 14 Appendix A.2; pinned HybridBatchNorm.forward, Client.buffer_update, Sever.aggregate_only_buffer, FedHBN_main.py
claim.text: The released method obtains the global feature moments required by the unbiased pooled-statistics argument.

assumptions: Two fully participating clients with 64 scalar activations each.
32 values of 8 and 32 of 12 in each client, all included in the first batch.
Constructor global mean 0, variance 1, alpha 0; cleared running buffers; server momentum 1.
problems.check: Independent literal scalar arithmetic and static call-path inspection.
problems.result: Reported mean 5 versus true 10; reported variance 320/127 versus required 512/127.
counterevidence: Separate collection pass and server between-client variance term are implemented.
Correct pooled identity remains valid for raw moments.
Historical experiments are not version-bound to this release.
problems.impact: Material failure of the central exact-statistics component in the pinned implementation, including evaluation recalibration. No empirical score loss inferred.
problems.correction: Collect raw moments consistently across layers and sampling schemes; identify historical revision and verify affected evaluations.
problems.core_dependency: Central exact global-statistics claim and evaluation recalibration use the collection/aggregation path.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: fully observed two-client example passes hybrid moments instead of raw moments and yields wrong pooled statistics.

acceptance_check.scope: Pooling identity remains correct for raw common features; historical empirical effects unknown.

claim.location: PDF page 13 Appendix A.1 Equation (14) and final paragraph
claim.text: Absolute aggregate discrepancy equals average absolute discrepancy and increases with heterogeneity.

assumptions: f(w,x)=w; equal client sizes; local quadratic losses with targets +/-1; initial weight 0; learning rate 1.
problems.check: Compute local weights +/-1 and global weight 0.
problems.result: Printed equality has left side 0 and right side 1; scaling targets preserves zero aggregate discrepancy.
counterevidence: Appendix A.2 pooled identity survives with correct grouping.
Actual source page14 visual inspection disproves the prior report's duplicate-Nk accusation: the between-client term lies outside the inner i-sum. No duplicate-count counterexample applies.
problems.impact: Overstated motivating argument, not a refutation of pooling or all empirical results.
problems.correction: Use triangle inequality and qualify monotonicity/sampling claims. In Equation (16)'s first variance line place indexed Nk inside the k-sum; the subsequent grouped expansion already has the between-client term outside the inner i-sum.
problems.core_dependency: Appendix A.1 motivating discrepancy argument, separate from valid raw-moment pooling.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: cancellation invalidates the absolute-value equality and universal monotonicity. Actual p.14 image refutes the prior report's duplicate-Nk summation accusation.

acceptance_check.scope: Use triangle inequality; withdraw duplicate-count claim. First-line free-index placement is a local notation issue; subsequent grouped pooling expansion is valid.

Identify historical revision, repetitions, checkpoint/grid selection split, FixBN learning-rate discrepancy, and momentum 0.002 versus 0.01.
